title: Active encounters not filtered by focused location
description: locationEncounters.active in GameView.tsx filters only by status === 'active' without checking if the encounter belongs to the focused location. Shows ALL active encounters from every location when viewing any single location.
evidence: GameView.tsx lines 166-168: gameState.encounterProgress.filter(p => p.status === 'active') — missing p.locationId === focusedLocation.id check
suggestedFix: Add location filter: gameState.encounterProgress.filter(p => p.status === 'active' && p.locationId === focusedLocation.id)

title: Threat badge backgrounds exceed Threadbare brightness ceiling for non-magic UI elements
description: STYLE.md mandates non-magic world surfaces stay in 10-40% brightness. Threat badges are UI chrome, not magic elements, but their backgrounds are at L=56% (moderate/amber) and L=68% (easy/blue), well above the 40% ceiling. THREAT_RATING_COLORS range L=56-71%, all violating brightness ceiling when used as solid fill backgrounds.
evidence: moderate badge bg: #fbbf24 HSL(43,96%,56%). easy badge bg: #60a5fa HSL(213,94%,68%). STYLE.md rule: 'world's value range is 10-40% brightness.'
suggestedFix: Use threat colors at low opacity for backgrounds: backgroundColor: threatColor + '20' (12% alpha) with full-brightness color as text. Or use as text/border on dark bg: backgroundColor: 'var(--bg-deep)', color: threatColor, border: '1px solid ' + threatColor + '66'.

title: Two encounter templates reference non-existent LocationSubtypes 'library' and 'cave'
description: encounter.scholar_aid uses locationTypes: ['library', 'ruins', 'temple'] and encounter.sanctuary_construction uses locationTypes: ['cave', 'mining', 'unexplored_poi']. Neither 'library' nor 'cave' exist in the LocationSubtype union type (src/types/index.ts:50-56). These templates will never match any location, making them unreachable content.
evidence: encounter-content.ts line 2974: 'library'. Line 3629: 'cave'. LocationSubtype union has 20 values, neither includes 'library' or 'cave'. locationTypes typed as string[] instead of LocationSubtype[] allows this to compile.
suggestedFix: Replace 'library' with 'temple' or 'ruins', 'cave' with 'mining' or 'ruins'. Then fix locationTypes type to LocationSubtype[] to prevent recurrence.

title: Encounter engine mutates state in-place
description: encounter.ts directly mutates state arrays and objects: state.encounterProgress.push() (line 101), progress.history.push() (line 221), progress.currentEncounterIndex++ (line 231), progress.status = 'completed'/'abandoned' (lines 234/238). Violates React immutability expectations.
evidence: Lines 101, 221, 229-238 in encounter.ts use direct mutation instead of returning new objects
suggestedFix: Return new state objects from initiateEncounter/advanceEncounter/abandonEncounter instead of mutating inputs. Use spread operators and array concat.

title: locationTypes typed as string[] instead of LocationSubtype[]
description: EncounterTemplate.locationTypes is typed as string[] (encounter.ts:117) instead of LocationSubtype[]. This allows invalid subtypes like 'library' and 'cave' to compile without error, hiding content bugs. The type system should catch these at compile time.
evidence: src/types/encounter.ts line 117: locationTypes: string[]. Should be LocationSubtype[] from src/types/index.ts
suggestedFix: Change to locationTypes: LocationSubtype[] and fix the two templates with invalid subtypes.

title: Encounter names use body font instead of display font
description: Encounter template names like 'The Spirit Walk' are narrative proper nouns — should use Cinzel (var(--font-display)) consistent with location name styling. Currently render in Alegreya Sans (body font). Section headings 'Encounters' correctly use Cinzel, but encounter names within cards do not — visual hierarchy inversion.
evidence: Encounter name fontFamily: Alegreya Sans (var(--font-body)). Compare: 'Sacred Grove' h2 fontFamily: Cinzel (var(--font-display)).
suggestedFix: Add fontFamily: 'var(--font-display)' to encounter name elements in both files.

title: Threat badge white text on bright backgrounds violates Threadbare aesthetic
description: Threat badges use color: 'white' (#ffffff, L=100%) as text on bright saturated backgrounds (moderate=#fbbf24 L=56%, easy=#60a5fa L=68%). Creates a bright-on-bright pairing that violates Threadbare principle of keeping non-magic elements subdued. Badges are UI chrome, not magic.
evidence: Badge text: #ffffff L=100%. Badge bg moderate: #fbbf24 L=56%. Badge bg easy: #60a5fa L=68%.
suggestedFix: Invert badge design: dark background with threat color as text and 1px border. E.g., backgroundColor: 'var(--bg-deep)', color: threatColor, border: '1px solid ' + threatColor.

title: No feedback when clicking unfamiliar agent in LocationView
description: Clicking an agent calls onAgentClick but if familiarity is 'Stranger' (default), getAgentInfoCard() returns null and sidebar stays on RetinuePanel. No visual feedback tells user why nothing happened.
evidence: useAgentInteraction.ts lines 94-99: agentInfoCard gated by familiarity. LocationView agent button shows 'active' state but sidebar doesn't change for unfamiliar agents.
suggestedFix: Show brief toast/tooltip 'You don't know this agent well enough yet' when clicking unfamiliar agent, or dim unfamiliar agent rows with a lock icon.

title: handleHexClickMove depends on entire gameState object
description: handleHexClickMove useCallback has gameState in dependency array, causing callback to recreate on every tick since gameState changes each tick.
evidence: useViewNavigation.ts line 130: [moveMode, gameState, handleHexClick, COLS, ROWS, setGameState]
suggestedFix: Destructure gameState.graph, gameState.ascendantId, gameState.visibilityMap, gameState.tick and use those in dependency array.

title: Buttons show default cursor instead of pointer
description: Agent buttons in LocationView render with cursor: default instead of cursor: pointer, making them look non-interactive.
evidence: Browser computed style shows cursor: default on agent button elements
suggestedFix: Add cursor: 'pointer' to button style or className 'cursor-pointer'.

title: Inconsistent threat badge border-radius between EncounterLog and LocationView
description: EncounterLog uses rounded-full (pill, 9999px) for threat badges while LocationView uses rounded (4px). Same data type should have consistent shape.
evidence: EncounterLog.tsx line 56: rounded-full (9999px). LocationView.tsx line 276: rounded (4px).
suggestedFix: Standardize on rounded (4px) for both — pills feel out of place in angular Threadbare UI.

title: Encounter type/reach labels lack semantic color differentiation
description: Type/reach labels (e.g., 'explore . veil') are flat var(--text-tertiary). Reach names have canonical colors in STYLE.md's Nine Reaches table. Using reach domain tint would add visual information.
evidence: All type/reach labels: #8a7e70 L=49%. Nine Reaches canonical colors: Veil=#4a9b8e, Flesh=#b07850 etc. not used.
suggestedFix: Split label into two spans — encounter type in var(--text-tertiary), reach name in its canonical reach color.

title: Agents Present column visually sparse compared to Encounters column
description: Two-column layout shows significant visual imbalance. Left column often has 1 agent (~60px) then ~400px blank space. Right has 5 encounter cards + overflow.
evidence: Visual weight ratio approximately 1:5 between columns.
suggestedFix: Add location description/flavor text below agents list, or location details section showing terrain, sphere influence data.

title: Encounter card padding inconsistency between active and available cards
description: EncounterLog (active) uses p-4 (16px) while LocationView available cards use px-3 py-2 (12px/8px). Different internal spacing for same encounter data type.
evidence: EncounterLog.tsx line 32: p-4 (16px). LocationView.tsx line 261: px-3 py-2 (8px 12px).
suggestedFix: Standardize on px-3 py-2.5 for both, or document as intentional hierarchy in ui-patterns.md.

title: Status indicators use hardcoded hex colors instead of CSS variables
description: EncounterLog uses Unicode characters for status with inline hardcoded colors (#4ade80 green, #ef4444 red) bypassing the CSS custom property system used elsewhere.
evidence: EncounterLog.tsx line 68: color: '#4ade80'. Line 71: color: '#ef4444'. Not CSS vars.
suggestedFix: Replace with small colored div circles (like step dots) using CSS vars or THREAT_RATING_COLORS.trivial for success green.

title: Available encounter card names at L=85% compete with location title
description: Available encounter names use var(--text-primary) at L=85%, same brightness as location title. These are secondary browsable info, not primary heading. Names are brighter than their own section heading.
evidence: Encounter name: #e8dcc8 L=85% = var(--text-primary). Section heading 'Encounters': #b8a890 L=64% (var(--text-secondary)).
suggestedFix: Change available encounter names from var(--text-primary) to var(--text-secondary). Keep var(--text-primary) for active encounter names in EncounterLog.

title: Agent button missing aria-label
description: Agent buttons in LocationView have no aria-label, relying only on visual text for screen reader identification.
evidence: LocationView.tsx line 148: <button> has no aria-label attribute
suggestedFix: Add aria-label={`View ${agent.name}, ${actorType}`}.

title: No focus ring on interactive elements
description: Agent buttons and back button have no visible focus ring outline for keyboard navigation.
evidence: No outline or focus:ring class on agent buttons
suggestedFix: Add focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-[var(--accent-gold)].

title: LocationView not wrapped in React.memo
description: LocationView receives array and function props from GameView but is not wrapped in React.memo, causing unnecessary re-renders.
evidence: LocationView.tsx line 22: export function LocationView — no React.memo
suggestedFix: Wrap with React.memo.

title: Inline getAgentName prop creates new reference each render
description: GameView passes inline arrow function for getAgentName prop to LocationView.
evidence: GameView.tsx line 455: getAgentName={(id) => gameState.graph.getNode(id)?.name ?? 'Unknown'}
suggestedFix: Extract to useCallback.

title: encounter.ts references non-existent state.traceBuffer property
description: Three emitTrace calls in encounter.ts use 'id: state.traceBuffer?.length ?? 0' but GameState has no traceBuffer property. emitTrace() overrides the id field anyway (traceBuffer.ts assigns auto-incrementing ids). This is dead code that suggests a misunderstanding of the trace architecture.
evidence: encounter.ts lines 105, 177, 242: state.traceBuffer?.length ?? 0. GameState type has no traceBuffer field. emitTrace() ignores the id field.
suggestedFix: Remove the id field from trace objects — emitTrace assigns ids automatically.

title: encounterProgress array grows unboundedly
description: encounterProgress only adds entries (push) and never removes completed/abandoned ones. Over a long game (hundreds of ticks), the array grows without bound, causing progressively slower .find()/.filter()/.some() operations in hot paths (phaseEncounterProgression, LocationView rendering).
evidence: encounter.ts line 101: state.encounterProgress.push(progress). No pruning of completed entries anywhere.
suggestedFix: Add periodic pruning of completed/abandoned entries older than N ticks, or move them to a separate completedEncounters array that isn't scanned in hot paths.

title: Step progress dots lack accessible labeling
description: EncounterLog step progress dots are visual-only divs with no accessible text. Screen readers cannot communicate which step is current or total step count.
evidence: EncounterLog step dots: <div> elements with background color only, no aria-label or sr-only text
suggestedFix: Add aria-label='Step N of M' or sr-only span with step count.

title: Inline onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave hover handlers
description: Agent buttons use inline arrow functions for hover state that create new closures on every render.
evidence: LocationView.tsx lines 150-155: onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave inline handlers
suggestedFix: Replace with CSS hover pseudo-class or extract handlers to module level.

title: Duplicate location type resolution logic
description: Both getAvailableEncounters and generateEncountersForLocation resolve location type via identical property access pattern.
evidence: encounter.ts lines 68 and 277-280 contain identical property access
suggestedFix: Extract getLocationSubtype(node) helper.

title: No trace emission in encounterCandidates.ts
description: encounterCandidates.ts generates and filters encounter candidates using personality-weighted scoring, but emits no traces. This makes the candidate selection pipeline opaque in the debug panel — you can't see why a particular encounter was chosen or filtered out.
evidence: encounterCandidates.ts has no emitTrace calls. Compare: agentSelection.ts emits action_selection traces with 5-stage pipeline snapshots.
suggestedFix: Add encounter_candidates trace with candidate count, filtered count, top-scored candidate, and personality weights used.

title: Establishing shot placeholder could use sphere-colored accent
description: Placeholder area is purely neutral. Other placeholders in the game use sphere-colored accents. A subtle sphere-colored border would tie into theming.
evidence: Container: bg=#222228, border=#2a2520. No sphere accent unlike other interactive placeholders.
suggestedFix: Add subtle top border using location's dominant sphere color at low opacity.

title: Available encounter cards lack hover state
description: Available encounter cards are plain divs with no hover effect or cursor change. Agent rows in left column have hover states — right column inconsistently does not.
evidence: LocationView.tsx lines 257-293: no onClick, no cursor-pointer, no hover state on encounter cards.
suggestedFix: Add subtle hover styling or cursor-default with transition-colors to signal status.

title: '+N more available' overflow is non-interactive
description: When more than 5 encounters are available, overflow text is plain italic with no way to see hidden encounters.
evidence: LocationView.tsx lines 296-305: availableEncounters.slice(0, 5) with static overflow text
suggestedFix: Make overflow text a clickable 'Show all' toggle or add scrollable container.
